Anchor:
Drives:
- keeping their community stable
- being the person others rely on
- preserving what works

Traits:
- steady under pressure
- remembers everyone's business
- stubborn about routines

Morality: loyalty to the neighborhood first

Relationships:
- the one people come to with problems
- earns trust through consistency
- slow to accept outsiders
Arena Soul:
Drives:
- testing themselves against worthy opponents
- earning respect through skill and will
- staying match-ready

Traits:
- reads a fight before it starts
- direct and physical in all things
- respects effort over status

Morality: the bout is honest even when the world is not

Relationships:
- bonds through shared training
- judges people by what they can back up
- loyal to coaches and sparring partners
Broker:
Drives:
- knowing what everyone needs
- being owed favors
- staying connected

Traits:
- remembers every deal and slight
- reads a room before speaking
- keeps their own needs private

Morality: a deal honored is worth more than a friend gained

Relationships:
- cultivates useful contacts across houses
- trades access for loyalty
- never fully trusts anyone who cannot offer something
Builder:
Drives:
- solving problems with tools and method
- making things that work
- understanding how systems fit together

Traits:
- thinks in steps and tolerances
- impatient with guesswork
- proud of clean work

Morality: if it is built right it will hold

Relationships:
- respects competence above rank
- teaches by showing rather than telling
- trusts people who maintain their own gear
Caretaker:
Drives:
- making sure others are safe and fed
- preventing harm before it arrives
- being needed

Traits:
- notices discomfort before it is mentioned
- firm about what people need versus what they want
- exhausts themselves last

Morality: protect first and ask why later

Relationships:
- earns devotion through attention
- expects their care to be accepted
- struggles to let people fail on their own
Climber:
Drives:
- rising in standing and influence
- being recognized by those above them
- never going back to where they started

Traits:
- tracks status and hierarchy instinctively
- adapts behavior to the audience
- works harder than anyone sees

Morality: ambition is not a vice if the results are real

Relationships:
- cultivates mentors and sponsors
- measures friendships partly by usefulness
- generous to those who supported them early
Cynic:
Drives:
- seeing through pretense
- refusing to be fooled again
- surviving on low expectations

Traits:
- sharp-tongued and observant
- assumes the worst explanation first
- occasionally right in ways that matter

Morality: honesty is the only kindness left

Relationships:
- pushes people away with criticism
- secretly values the ones who stay
- respects anyone who proves them wrong
Devotee:
Drives:
- serving a cause or principle larger than themselves
- converting doubt into conviction
- living as proof that the cause works

Traits:
- unwavering under opposition
- sees choices through the lens of the cause
- patient with honest questions but not with mockery

Morality: the principle is right even when the outcome hurts

Relationships:
- bonds deeply with fellow believers
- respects sincere disagreement more than apathy
- will sacrifice a friendship to keep a conviction
Drifter:
Drives:
- staying unattached
- finding the next place or opportunity
- avoiding the obligations that come with staying

Traits:
- adapts quickly to new people and places
- travels light in possessions and commitments
- hard to pin down on plans

Morality: freedom is worth more than comfort

Relationships:
- makes friends easily and leaves them behind
- shows up unexpectedly and is welcome for a while
- keeps one or two distant connections alive
Enforcer:
Drives:
- maintaining order in their jurisdiction
- being the line between safe and not safe
- following the chain of command

Traits:
- reads threats by habit
- economical with words
- uncomfortable with ambiguity in authority

Morality: the rules exist for a reason

Relationships:
- trusts their unit above civilians
- respects those who cooperate without being asked
- judges hesitation as a potential problem
Free Agent:
Drives:
- working for themselves on their own terms
- building a reputation worth hiring
- answering to nobody permanently

Traits:
- self-reliant and resourceful
- negotiates everything
- takes professional pride in finishing the job

Morality: a contract is a contract

Relationships:
- keeps clients and colleagues separate from friends
- loyal to repeat employers who pay fair
- wary of anyone offering a permanent position
Frontier Hand:
Drives:
- getting the work done with what is available
- surviving conditions that would break a city dweller
- proving they belong where comfort ends

Traits:
- practical and physically capable
- reads weather and terrain before people
- impatient with complaints about hardship

Morality: pull your weight or get out of the way

Relationships:
- bonds fast with people who share the work
- mistrusts anyone who has never been uncomfortable
- protective of crew and settlement
Handler:
Drives:
- keeping systems running and organized
- anticipating failures before they happen
- being the person who knows where everything is

Traits:
- methodical and detail-oriented
- prefers procedure to improvisation
- stressed by things outside their control

Morality: competence is a form of care

Relationships:
- earns trust by never losing track of anything
- frustrated by people who skip steps
- quietly indispensable to those around them
House Loyalist:
Drives:
- serving their house and its standing
- embodying the values they were raised in
- earning their place through dedication

Traits:
- carries house identity in posture and speech
- reads inter-house dynamics automatically
- defensive when house honor is questioned

Morality: the house made me and I will not betray it

Relationships:
- bonds tightest within house structures
- evaluates outsiders by their house or lack of one
- respects loyalty even in a rival house
Hustler:
Drives:
- finding the angle nobody else sees
- staying ahead of trouble
- turning nothing into something

Traits:
- fast-talking and quick to pivot
- bends rules rather than breaking them
- always working more than one scheme

Morality: everyone is playing a game whether they admit it or not

Relationships:
- charms people into short-term alliances
- drops contacts who become liabilities
- secretly grateful to anyone who helps without an angle
Investigator:
Drives:
- understanding how things actually work
- following evidence wherever it leads
- not settling for the first explanation

Traits:
- asks questions others find uncomfortable
- patient with complexity
- remembers contradictions

Morality: the truth matters even when it is inconvenient

Relationships:
- earns trust through thoroughness
- unnerves people who prefer surfaces
- values collaborators who bring evidence not opinions
Operator:
Drives:
- running their business cleanly and profitably
- maintaining a reputation that keeps them alive
- staying invisible to the wrong people

Traits:
- calm under pressure
- calculates risk before acting
- never makes a threat they cannot follow through

Morality: the underground has rules and breaking them gets people killed

Relationships:
- separates personal from professional absolutely
- rewards reliability and punishes loose talk
- respects other professionals regardless of legality
Pedagogue:
Drives:
- passing on what they know
- maintaining standards in their field
- shaping the next generation of practitioners

Traits:
- explains by building from what the listener knows
- holds students to higher standards than strangers
- protective of their discipline

Morality: knowledge given carelessly does more harm than knowledge withheld

Relationships:
- bonds through mentorship
- proudest of students who surpass them
- impatient with talent that will not work
Performer:
Drives:
- being seen and remembered
- expressing what others cannot articulate
- perfecting their craft

Traits:
- aware of audience at all times
- shifts energy to fill or calm a room
- takes criticism of their work personally

Morality: authenticity in expression justifies risk

Relationships:
- draws people in easily
- needs recognition more than they admit
- most honest when performing and most guarded when not
Professional:
Drives:
- doing the job correctly every time
- being recognized as competent by peers
- upholding the standards of their trade

Traits:
- methodical and reliable
- proud without being showy
- uncomfortable cutting corners

Morality: good work speaks for itself

Relationships:
- respects fellow professionals regardless of field
- judges people by whether they take their work seriously
- loyal to employers who let them do the job right
Recluse:
Drives:
- being left alone
- maintaining their own space and boundaries
- understanding something deeply without interruption

Traits:
- private and self-contained
- surprisingly knowledgeable about narrow subjects
- uncomfortable in crowds or forced sociability

Morality: my business is mine and yours is yours

Relationships:
- tolerates a small number of people who respect their space
- communicates best in practical exchanges
- withdraws rather than confronts
Reformer:
Drives:
- changing something they believe is broken
- convincing others the cost of change is worth it
- refusing to accept that this is just how things are

Traits:
- articulate about what is wrong
- impatient with incrementalism
- risks their own standing for the argument

Morality: the system owes people better than this

Relationships:
- rallies allies around shared frustration
- alienates people who benefit from the status quo
- respects anyone willing to act on conviction
